messages:
sophie_cs: Forwarding a customer report received this morning. They say after last night's rollout the Mandarin/Cantonese responses flip dialects, tone became casual, and a few requests returned 502 when they set Accept-Language: zh-HK. Customer pasted examples and a curl repro.

sophie_cs: CUSTOMER QUOTE:
> We used to get Traditional Cantonese (formal) for zh-HK. After the deploy responses are half Cantonese, half Simplified Mandarin, and the tone is now 'chatty' — not acceptable for our checkout flow. Also see intermittent 502s when locale header is zh-HK.

sophie_cs: Repro from customer (redacted):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "Accept-Language: zh-HK" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"請把這段文字翻成繁體臺灣用語，正式一點，用於收銀頁面"}]}'
```
They send back either a Cantonese/formal translation OR a Simplified Mandarin casual one. Sample responses below.

sophie_cs: EXPECTED (from pre-rollout):
> 您好，請將下列文字翻譯為繁體中文（臺灣用語），並保持正式語氣，用於結帳頁面。

sophie_cs: GOT (post-rollout):
> 你好，把這段文字翻成簡體中文就好啦，結帳流程沒問題。

sophie_cs: They attached one request id for a 502: request_id=rid_9f2b3c1, timestamp 2026-02-12T01:14:22Z. Said the 502s happen ~5% of zh-HK requests since deploy.

anika_support: Thanks Sophie. Can you paste the full request payload + headers (no auth) and customer org id? Also which model was being used (if they reported)?

sophie_cs: Sent org id privately. They say model: redwood/phoenix-1:2026-02-11 (we asked them to confirm). I'll paste a minimal payload: same as curl above.

matt_eng: :eyes: This looks like a routing/model-selection problem or prompt-preprocessing change. Two hypotheses: (1) a new locale-routing rule started mapping zh-HK to zh-CN model variant fallback, or (2) quantized fallback model has different tokenizer/config that normalizes to simplified and more casual completions.

matt_eng: Can we check the smart-routing logs for that org around the rid_9f2b3c1 and see which model instance handled it? Also check feature-flag state for locale-normalization rolled out in the same deploy.

kai_sre: I'll grab the routing traces. If 502s are appearing only when Accept-Language=zh-HK, maybe a header parsing change triggered an upstream service to drop connection. I want: request_id, route decision, backend instance id, and upstream error.

deploy-bot: Deploy completed: release/2026-02-11-translate-fix (sha: a1b2c3d) at 2026-02-11T23:58:10Z. Flags toggled: locale-normalization=true for 20% of traffic, routing-fallback=auto.

anika_support: Flag note is important — 20% rollouts could explain partial regressions. Sophie: did customer see intermittent behavior (some requests good, some bad) or all requests changed?

sophie_cs: They said intermittent — roughly 1-in-20 requests were wrong/different, and ~5% 502s. They only started after deploy on 02-11.

matt_eng: Action items:
- Check routing logs for sample rids (kai).
- Check which model variant (full vs fallback/quant) served zh-HK.
- Roll back locale-normalization flag for affected region if it's tied to behavior.
- Get a minimal repro we can hit internally (I'll run same curl with Accept-Language header).

kai_sre: Pulling logs now. If we see backend oom or TLS reset, I'll correlate to the 502 spike. Also will confirm whether the locale-normalization service is throwing exceptions for zh-HK header tokenization.

anika_support: I'll request a few more request_ids and timestamps from the customer and ask them to send a short golden-pair (expected vs received) for 5 samples so we can do regression diffs.

sophie_cs: Customer sent two more rids: rid_9f2b3c2, rid_9f2b3d8 (timestamps 2026-02-12T01:16Z and 01:20Z). Also attached a screencap showing '簡體' characters in their web UI.

matt_eng: Thanks. If routing isn't the issue, next suspect is tokenizer/normalizer introduced in locale-normalization. That component can map Traditional->Simplified for certain locales if misconfigured. I'll grep the feature-flag rollout commit for any mapping tables touching zh-HK.

kai_sre: Found an error pattern: upstream translator-worker returned 502 when header included hyphenated locale values (zh-HK) but worked for zh_HK and zh_Hans. Looks like a header parsing regex changed in release. Correlating to rid_9f2b3c1's trace now.

matt_eng: That's promising — header parsing bug explains 502s. But the dialect flip still needs explaining: if locale-normalization mapped zh-HK -> zh-Hans then we get Simplified outputs. That could be a mapping table bug.

anika_support: Suggest we throttle locale-normalization rollout to 0% for APAC until fix. Sophie, can you request customer tolerance for a short rollback window? We'll need to inform them and schedule rollback with SRE.

sophie_cs: Customer prefers immediate stability. They've agreed to a rollback if we can do it quickly.

matt_eng: Ok I'll open a rollback PR and coordinate with Kai for a quick revert of the flag and the regex change. Also need to add unit test for header formats with hyphen vs underscore and a test for zh-HK mapping.

kai_sre: Planning a quick rollback at 2026-02-12T03:00Z unless we find a hotfix. Will monitor 502s post-rollback.

anika_support: I'll update the customer and ask for the 5 sample pairs. Also prepping a postmortem template.

sophie_cs: :thumbsup: Thanks team. Will ping when customer confirms rollback is acceptable and once they send samples.

matt_eng: Logging owner: @matt_eng. I'll take postmortem write-up after fix.

kai_sre: Added alert: increased 502 rate for Accept-Language header matching /zh[-_]HK/i. Monitoring dashboard updated. :bar_chart:
